title: Unknown writer to 'Monsieur', 17th c., French homophonic pigpen, TNA SP 106/10 ff. 241-243 (DECODE R927)

steps.what: Pencil flap key and all grid orientations/dot orders tested
Homophonic annealing (hc3.py) lands on French; anchors fixed by hand
f. 243 read almost in full, f. 241 in fragments

Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): the letter was decoded by Sheila Richards in Secret Writings (1973). Not found by the Sept 2026 web search; not seen, not used. Independent re-solution, dropped from the ciphertext-only list for Klaus Schmeh.

outcome.method_basis: The homophonic pigpen key was built by annealing (hc3.py) on a hand transcription of f. 243 until French emerged, then fixed with guessed anchors ('monsieur', 'vous supplie'); the pencil key on the flap was tested and rejected, and no prior solution was found at the time; Lasry later reported it decoded by Sheila Richards in Secret Writings (1973), so this is an independent re-solution.
outcome.notes: Last page read, first page in fragments, second page not transcribed. fraction_read is an estimate from the NOTES, not measured.

gaps.detail: auto-segmentation too noisy, full hand transcription not done

gaps.item: the two circle/"9" signs and stacked composites on f. 243
gaps.detail: they sit where names or abbreviations are expected, too few to value
expected in the unread start of the letter

outcome.fraction_read_source: p3_plain.txt covers f. 243 only; ff. 241-242 were never transcribed, so the letter's token total cannot be counted

prior.where: Sheila Richards, Secret Writings (1973), as reported by G. Lasry (email 25 Sept 2026); the book was not seen here and a web search found no bibliographic record.
